summary:
Saarland has no trans-specific statute of its own. Its state constitution was amended in 2011 so that its anti-discrimination provisions explicitly include sexual orientation and gender identity, one of five Länder constitutions to carry such a clause. The consequence for a visitor is that transphobic hate speech is prohibited under Saarland's constitution, while hate speech on the basis of sexual orientation and gender identity is not banned nationwide.

Prison placement in Saarland is governed by the national framework because the state has enacted no placement statute of its own; the legal gender entry is the default basis for placement unless a state law provides otherwise. A constitutional-law analysis published on 18 March 2026 cites Saarland's single-cell accommodation with en-suite shower as a positive practice model for trans inmates. The same analysis records that constitutional law does not oblige authorities to follow the legal gender entry, so the default in Saarland is a practice rather than an enforceable guarantee.
tangentialFactors:
Saarland's protection against discrimination on gender identity rests on its constitution rather than on trans-specific legislation. Legislative activity on trans prison placement in other Länder has not been matched in Saarland, which has no placement statute.

Saarland was among the Länder that tabled the joint Bundesrat motion for a ban on conversion therapy, presented in plenary on 12 April 2019. The ban that followed was enacted federally rather than by Saarland.
localsOnly:
The 2011 amendment to Saarland's constitution makes sexual orientation and gender identity explicit grounds in its anti-discrimination provisions. The clause binds state authorities and is the basis for the state's prohibition of transphobic hate speech.

People held in Saarland's prisons are accommodated under the state's single-cell-with-en-suite-shower model, cited in the March 2026 analysis as a positive practice for trans inmates.
outOfScopeNotes:
No Saarland-specific record of enforcement of the constitutional prohibition of transphobic hate speech was identified: no prosecutions, complaints or court decisions from Saarland appear in the sources.

The single-cell accommodation model is cited in a legal commentary rather than in a court ruling or a statement by the Saarland prison service, and no account of its application to an individual trans prisoner in Saarland was identified.

No Saarland-specific statute, ordinance or administrative rule on trans prison placement was identified; the state's position is defined by the absence of such a rule.
